property_summary: For any caller and any msg.value, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) while the mutant unconditionally sets it to block.timestamp, so there exist inputs (where _unlockTime > block.timestamp) that make the mutant differ.

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, calling Put(_unlockTime) sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp and if _unlockTime > block.timestamp then Acc[caller].unlockTime == _unlockTime in the reference; the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after Put(...) completes the reference ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp and equals _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the mutant that always writes block.timestamp violates this whenever the caller supplies _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp and if caller supplied _unlockTime > block.timestamp then Acc[caller].unlockTime equals that supplied _unlockTime; the mutant that always writes block.timestamp breaks this whenever the fuzz provides an _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and provided _unlockTime, after Put(_unlockTime) the reference sets Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least block.timestamp and specifically to _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp; the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp violates this for some inputs where _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any sent value and unlockTime, after calling Put(unlockTime) the stored Acc[msg.sender].unlockTime in the reference contract is always >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime to a past timestamp), whereas the mutant can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus violate this invariant.

After any call to Put by any address with any ether and any _unlockTime, the reference contract always stores Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp, while the mutant can set Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs.

For any caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures that immediately after Put returns the stored Acc[caller].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp, while the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime (a past timestamp).

For every call to Put by any caller with any ether and any _unlockTime, the reference contract ensures that after Put returns Acc[caller].unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (it never sets unlockTime into the past); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make Acc[caller].unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For every call to Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures Acc[caller].unlockTime >= block.timestamp after the call; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime (a past timestamp), breaking this invariant.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, a successful Put call on the reference contract always leaves the contract unlocked (allowing a subsequent Put to succeed); the mutant that omits re-lock reset keeps locked_ true after Put, causing subsequent Put calls to revert for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount that meets the contract's MinSum requirement, two sequential successful Put calls from the same caller must both succeed on the reference (the contract does not remain permanently locked after Put), whereas the mutant that omits re-lock reset leaves the contract locked after the first call and causes the second Put to revert for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, two sequential Put calls by the same caller should both succeed on the reference (locked_ is cleared after the first call), whereas the mutant that omits resetting locked_ will leave the contract locked and make the second Put revert for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero payable amount, after a single successful Put(...) the reference contract remains unlocked so that a second Put(...) from the same caller with the same admissible amount also succeeds; the mutant that omits re-lock reset leaves the contract permanently locked after the first call and thus makes the second Put revert for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any admissible single Put call (any payable amount >=0 and any _unlockTime), the reference contract leaves locked_ == false after Put returns so a subsequent zero-value fallback-triggered Put (via sending plain Ether with empty calldata) will succeed; the mutant that omits re-lock reset keeps locked_ true and causes that subsequent fallback-triggered Put to revert for some fuzzed inputs.

Invariant: After a successful Put(x) from any sender with any value ≥ MinSum, the sender's recorded balance in c.Acc(sender).balance equals the sent value added to their prior balance (i.e., Put is non-reentrant and always results in acc.balance += msg.value); the mutated contract allowing reentrancy can break this by enabling reentrant calls during Put that cause the stored balance to be inconsistent for some inputs.

For any caller, a single call to Put(value) atomically increases their recorded Acc balance by exactly msg.value (Acc(caller).balance after Put == prior balance + msg.value); removing the nonReentrant_ check allows a reentrant attacker to call Put recursively during execution and cause the final stored balance to be less than the sum, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For every caller and any payable amount, a single call to Put(...) always increases that caller's Acc balance by exactly msg.value (i.e., Acc(caller).balance after Put == prior balance + msg.value); removing the nonReentrant_ require allows a reentrant attacker to call back into Put during execution and can cause the final stored balance to be less than expected for some inputs.

For every caller and any payable amount, a single external Put(amount) call always increases that caller's recorded Acc balance by exactly msg.value (no reentrant interference); removing the initial nonReentrant_ require allows a reentrant attacker to call back into Put during its execution and break this atomicity for some inputs.

For every caller and payable amount, a single Put call always increases that caller's recorded Acc balance by exactly msg.value (i.e., Acc(caller).balance after Put == prior balance + msg.value); removing the nonReentrant_ require enables a reentrant attacker to reenter Put during execution and can make the final stored balance differ for some inputs.

Invariant: After a successful Collect by a holder, the holder's recorded balance in the contract strictly decreases by the collected amount; removing the reentrancy lock allows an attacker to reenter Collect during the external call and withdraw more than their original balance, violating this invariant.

For any holder and withdrawal amount, after calling Collect the contract's recorded holder balance is never negative and in the reference implementation a holder cannot extract more than their stored balance (i.e., Acc[holder].balance after Collect >= 0 and specifically decreased by at most the requested amount); removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw more than its original balance, violating that invariant.

For any holder address and withdrawal amount where the holder has at least MinSum and at least that amount and the unlock time passed, a single call to Collect on the reference cannot reduce the contract's balance (address(c).balance) below the sum of recorded balances in Acc for that holder (i.e., address(c).balance >= Acc[holder].balance), but removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to drain more and violate this relationship.

For any holder and withdraw amount, if the holder deposited at least MinSum and unlocked, then after calling Collect once the holder's recorded Acc[holder].balance is decreased by exactly the requested amount (i.e., Acc[holder].balance == originalBalance - requestedAmount); removing the reentrancy guard allows a reentrant attacker to call back into Collect during the external transfer and withdraw more than requested, breaking this equality.

For any holder, deposit amount, unlock time and withdrawal amount, if the holder deposited and is allowed to withdraw, then a single call to Collect cannot reduce the holder's recorded Acc balance by more than the requested withdrawal amount; removing the reentrancy guard allows a malicious contract to reenter during the external call and withdraw more than requested, breaking this bound.

The nonReentrant_ modifier on the reference blocks reentrant entry by requiring locked_==false (so Collect succeeds when called once and allows the external call to return normally), whereas the mutant inverts the require so calls are only allowed when locked_==true, making Collect revert for some legitimate callers — so for all inputs valid for reference, Collect does not revert, but the mutant causes Collect to revert for some inputs.

For any caller, amount and unlockTime, calling Collect from an account that previously deposited at least MinSum and waited past unlockTime should succeed (reference never reverts); the mutant inverting the nonReentrant_ require causes Collect to revert for some such inputs.

For any depositor who has balance >= MinSum and >= requested amount and whose unlockTime has passed, calling Collect should succeed (reference never reverts); the mutant inverting the nonReentrant_ require makes Collect revert for such valid calls for some inputs.

For any caller who previously deposited >= MinSum, requests to Collect an amount <= their balance after unlockTime should succeed on the reference (no revert); the mutant inverting the nonReentrant_ require causes such valid Collect calls to revert for some valid inputs.

For any caller who previously Put at least MinSum and whose unlockTime is in the past, calling Collect(...) never reverts on the reference contract, but the mutant that inverts nonReentrant_ will cause Collect to revert for some such valid inputs.
